**Swarms — insights** — what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the
roll-u

p and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| E
ndpoint | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat fail
ures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../g
oal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a f
inding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a s
warm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — sch

eduled, not done |
| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic trap

s worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the s

ession total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75% — not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGr
adingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a\n regression, and folding the two together makes one look like the oth

er.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —
`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *no
t* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring\nand dismissed, and hiding one neve

r claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on\
n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-
testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than\n> re-requesting; `force: true` delibe

rately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute
> brake (wait second
s), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403`

means
> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/
environments/{environmentId}/study`,\n`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, an
d controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exis

ts.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republis
hing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/stu
dy` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studie
s/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per se
ssion, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript,
paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visito
rs: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body
— the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `in
vited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending t

heir live sessions |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the
> old URL from granting NEW acce
ss; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotation\n>
is what you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not

intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpublishing, tighte
ning `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> stop

s working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read

`accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing — wha
t visitors did** — the analytics reads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are\nd

eterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/
metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .
../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate
|\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET
.../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/w
indows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .
../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the
window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId
` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it st

ays dismissed when insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usag
e` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` descri
be session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `st
aleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map indepe
ndently. Reading this response never starts analysis.\n\nTaxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme
ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unchan
ged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version

provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed c
ounts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather\nthan a fabricated map no

de.

The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open objects** on purpose.
Their upstream projections grow with the pr
oduct and the SDK types them the\nsame way, so pinning a field list would turn every new metric into a spec\nviolation. Read what

you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. P
oll the window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is\n> why it is never inf

erred from anything else.

**Feedback** — report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
\n| - | - |\n| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind,
